Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay. Blue skies greet the two umpires and players as they make their way out to the middle. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Fakhar Zaman ​​​​Abdullah Shafique to open the innings for Pakistan. Trent Boult is at the top of his mark and will start the proceedings for New Zealand. A slip in place. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

UPDATE - 3.08 pm IST (9.38 am GMT) - Good news! The rain has stopped and the covers have been removed. The ground staff are in the process of drying up the outfield to get the field ready for play. The match officials have decided that the Pakistan run chase will commence at 3.20 pm IST (9.50 am GMT).

UPDATE - 3.02 pm IST (9.32 am GMT) - The start of the chase might be a bit delayed as it is raining at the moment in Bangalore, but the sun is also out. So, the wait should not be that long. Stay with us for further updates.

Right then, New Zealand have batted Pakistan out of this game and they would want to bowl them out to boost their net run-rate significantly. As for Pakistan, they have their backs against the wall and will need to bat out of their skins to get anywhere close to the target. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

The centurion, Rachin Ravindra is up for a chat. He says that it is pretty surreal to play in the country of his background. Adds that it is always special to play in India, especially in Bangalore in front of his family. Tells that the wicket is a good one, it was a bit slow at the start but still good to bat on. Mentions that they can play freely upfront as they have good power hitters like Phillips, Mitchell and Santner who can make up in the end. Praises Kane Williamson for the way he batted and says that there wasn't a target in their mind and it was just about continuing to score runs at a good rate and use that impressive start. Ends by saying that they have managed to put a good total and hopes that it is enough.

Despite winning what was a crucial toss under overcast conditions, Shaheen Afridi failed to set the tone as he lacked rhythm, and it was the same with his new ball partner, Hasan Ali. They were all over the place with their lines and lengths and conceded boundaries every now and then. Pakistan looked completely flat during the middle phase, which was fairly dominated by the partnership between Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra. Having managed to dismiss both in the space of 10 balls, they sensed an opening to stage a comeback. However, they lacked consistency with their lines and lengths and allowed New Zealand to get away. Even in the last ten overs, they could not nail their deliveries and the slow over-rate penalty during the last three overs made matters even worse for them. On a day when Shaheen Afridi registered the most expensive figures by a Pakistani bowler in World Cups, Mohammad Wasim stood out for them with figures of 3 for 60 from his 10 overs.

New Zealand fall one short of their highest ODI total but this is their highest-ever World Cup total! Enough to tell you what kind of batting performance this has been from the Kiwis. After being sent into bat, New Zealand were off to a solid start with Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra getting into the groove quickly. Coming in at number 3, Kane Williamson got himself going with a couple of crisp boundaries and took the innings forward with Rachin Ravindra. The master and the apprentice looked at utmost ease in the middle during their 180-run stand. Although Williamson fell 5 runs short of his hundred, Ravindra brought up his third hundred and became the first batter to score three centuries in his maiden World Cup. After the departure of the two set batters, quickfire cameos from Daryl Mitchell, Mark Chapman and Glenn Phillips ensured that New Zealand did not lose their way at any stage. Not to forget, Mitchell Santner's unbeaten knock which took helped New Zealand cross 400.
Only a single to end the innings! Shaheen Afridi serves a low full toss, on middle, Mitchell Santner only manages to force it towards mid off for just a run. New Zealand finishes with 401/6!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! Pakistan players are spreading out to take their respective field positions. Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra are the two openers for New Zealand. Shaheen Afridi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that, players from both sides line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Pakistan's first followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

New Zealand's captain, Kane Williamson says that it is a slightly different looking surface than what it is usually here. Mentions that it is nice to be back and there are a few niggles in the camp. Adds that guys are excited for the challenge. Informs that they have made two changes to the side - Ish Sodhi comes in for Matt Henry and he comes in to replace Will Young. On Sodhi's inclusion, he says that they feel the surface might take turn throughout or even later in the game. Feels that it is important to stick to their plans and it will also be important to adapt to the conditions. Ends by saying that they will look to put up a competitive total on the board and defend later.

The skipper of Pakistan, Babar Azam says that they will bowl first. Adds that there is a bit of moisture on the wicket and that is the reason they are chasing here. Tells that their bowling has been good in the last couple of games and they are looking to continue that. Mentions that he is feeling good about his batting but he wants to finish the matches for the team. Informs Hasan Ali is in for Usama Mir.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Abdullah Shafique, Fakhar Zaman, Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Saud Shakeel, Iftikhar Ahmed, Agha Salman, Hasan Ali (In for Usama Mir), Shaheen Afridi, Mohammad Wasim, Haris Rauf.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra, Kane Williamson (C) (In for Will Young), Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (WK), Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman (In for James Neesham), Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi (In for Matt Henry), Tim Southee, Trent Boult.
TOSS - Babar Azam calls 'heads' and heads it is. Pakistan have opted to BOWL first.

After losing four of their first five games, Pakistan had their campaign sinking in front of their eyes. But thanks to South Africa's massive win over New Zealand and themselves winning emphatically over Bangladesh, there is light at the end of the tunnel for them. That said, their net run rate does not paint a promising picture, and Babar Azam's men will need to win big the next two matches. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are due for a big score, but Fakhar Zaman's timely inclusion has lessened their top-order woes. Shaheen Afridi has stood out, but not much support from the rest has been a cause for concern. Will Pakistan stake their claim for a semis spot with a win? Or will New Zealand return to winning ways? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up...

Having faltered at the final hurdle in 2019, New Zealand looked to be on a mission to go all the way this time with four wins in their first four matches. Then they suffered three losses in as many games and now find themselves in a not-so-comfortable position. The injury list continues to grow, but still, all is not lost for them, as two wins from their remaining two matches might be enough for them to seal a semi-final berth. With Matt Henry ruled out due to a hamstring strain, the veteran pace duo of Trent Boult and Tim Southee will have to do what they do best upfront. It was a disappointing batting effort for the Kiwis against South Africa, and the likes of Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra, and Daryl Mitchell will be looking to step up. Kane Williamson is close to being declared match-fit, and one feels that the return of their skipper might just be the boost New Zealand need.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of match number 35 of the 2023 ODI World Cup between New Zealand and Pakistan at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru. We are at that stage in the competition where every game holds significant importance, and this fixture is no exception, with so much riding on it for both teams who find their qualification hopes hanging in the balance.
... MATCH DAY ...

The battle to keep the World Cup semi-final hopes alive. Yes, Pakistan will meet New Zealand in Match No. 35, and it would seem to many of them that this would be a decisive game for the fourth spot. Afghanistan too are in contention but their last two games are against the mighty Aussies and the ferocious South Africans. So, coming to this game, many would have given up hope in Pakistan but they have felt a sudden lift in their step. Their actual semi-final qualification possibilities are dependent on several factors, but first, they must prevail handily in their next two games. They dominated Bangladesh by seven wickets in their previous match, securing their first victory after four straight defeats. Fakhar Zaman made a strong comeback against Bangladesh in the previous game and it would be interesting to see if Pakistan would consider him in this game as well. Their pace attack has been firing on all cylinders but they lack a quality spinner in the middle overs. They will need to find a way to overcome this. On the other hand, the Kiwis at the start were on a roll and had won four matches in a trot. However, a near defeat against India, a painful 5-run loss against the Aussies, and a thrashing 190-run loss against the Proteas have left them in a spot to bother. They cannot afford any more slip-ups and need to pull up now. This World Cup, Rachin Ravindra has been a standout performer for the Kiwis. Devon Conway has lost his touch in the last few games and the side would hope for him to put up a gritty stand alongside Will Young in this game. Matt Henry joins New Zealand's mounting injury list with a strained hamstring. Lockie Ferguson, who hurt his Achilles against Australia, will likely be fit for this game. New Zealand would have to bring their A game in this encounter and try to secure their place in the Semis. Can they do it? Or will Pakistan make an unexpected comeback? We shall find out as this game promises to be a cracker.
